items.aliasZh: 群青 · 佛青 · 天然群青 · 拉丁语意为「来自海那边」
items.aliasEn: Ultramarine · natural ultramarine · from lapis lazuli
items.histZh: 名字来自拉丁语 ultramarinus，「来自海的那一边」。颜料从阿富汗的萨里桑矿场出发，走陆路运到威尼斯，再由意大利商人分销全欧洲。文艺复兴时期它是画家里最贵的颜色，价格有时高过同等重量的黄金 —— 赞助人和画家签的合同里会专门为它单列一条，记录领用了几两、还剩多少。因为贵，它被默认留给最重要的地方：圣母的袍子。1826 年法国人吉梅用高岭土、硫磺和苏打烧出了人工群青，价格一落千丈，这种蓝才从奢侈品变成日常颜料。
items.histEn: The name comes from the Latin ultramarinus, meaning beyond the sea: the pigment travelled overland from the Sar-e-Sang mines of Afghanistan to Venice, and Italian traders distributed it across Europe. In the Renaissance it was the most expensive colour a painter could buy, at times valued above its weight in gold. Contracts and account books list it as a separate line item, recording how much was issued and how much was returned. Because it cost so much it was reserved for the most important passages, above all the robes of the Virgin. In 1826 the Frenchman Jean-Baptiste Guimet fired kaolin, sulfur and soda into synthetic ultramarine, the price collapsed, and the colour became ordinary.
items.funZh: 天然群青和人工群青在画家眼里是两个东西，分得很清。有记载说，一些画家宁可反复调整别的颜色，也不肯用群青去铺底，只在最后一两道罩染才舍得用它；而手里有天然群青的画家，会把它当作一笔资产写进遗嘱。
items.funEn: Painters treated natural and synthetic ultramarine as two different pigments and kept them strictly apart. Some would labour over every other colour rather than spend ultramarine on an underpainting, saving it for the final glazes; painters who owned a stock of the natural pigment sometimes listed it in their wills, like an asset.

items.aliasZh: 泰尔紫 · 帝王紫 · 骨螺紫 · 推罗紫
items.aliasEn: Tyrian purple · royal purple · murex purple
items.histZh: 从骨螺鳃下腺的分泌物里取得。常被引用的数字是：一克染料要上万只螺，而挤出来的黏液起初是白的，得靠日光氧化才慢慢转成紫。于是它在地中海世界几乎等同于权力本身 —— 罗马共和国有法律限定哪些等级的人才能穿，帝国时期更变成皇帝的垄断。制作过程的恶臭同样出名，染色工坊只能设在城外，否则城里人受不了。
items.histEn: It was extracted from the hypobranchial gland of murex sea snails. The figure usually quoted is that a single gram of dye took thousands of snails, and the secretion comes out white: only sunlight and air oxidise it into purple. Small wonder it came to mean power itself in the Mediterranean world. Republican Rome passed laws restricting who was allowed to wear it, and under the emperors it became a monopoly. The process stank so badly that dye works had to be sited outside the city walls.
items.funZh: 「皇家紫」这个词比染料活得久。骨螺紫会随光线和年份继续变化，从紫红一路走到暗棕，所以古代文献描述它时彼此矛盾：有人说像凝住的血，有人说是发黑的绛。今天波斯湾一带仍有人用古法染色，染出的布要先晒，颜色才慢慢出来。
items.funEn: The phrase royal purple outlived the snails by two thousand years. Murex purple keeps shifting with light and age, travelling from a purplish red toward a dark brown, which is why ancient writers describe it in contradictory terms: clotted blood in one account, a blackened crimson in another. Traditional dyeing with murex still continues around the Persian Gulf, and the cloth is hung in the sun before the colour appears.

items.aliasZh: 埃及蓝 · 硅酸铜钙 · 人类第一个合成颜料
items.aliasEn: Egyptian blue · calcium copper silicate · the first synthetic pigment
items.histZh: 把石英砂、石灰、铜（比如青铜屑）和碱一起烧到 900 度左右，得到一种硅酸铜钙晶体。这是目前已知人类第一次不靠天然矿物、自己造出来的颜料，比普鲁士蓝早四千多年。到公元前四世纪它已经横跨地中海，罗马人也在用；之后配方渐渐失传。十九世纪有人从庞贝的壁画上取下一小块重新分析成分，才把做法补回来 —— 现在实验室能按古法烧出它。
items.histEn: Grind quartz sand, lime, a copper source such as bronze filings and an alkali together, fire them at around 900 degrees, and you get a calcium copper silicate crystal. It is the earliest pigment humans are known to have made rather than dug up, more than four thousand years before Prussian blue. By the fourth century BCE it had spread across the Mediterranean and the Romans were using it; the recipe then faded out of knowledge. Only in the nineteenth century, when a fragment was taken from a wall painting at Pompeii and analysed, was the method pieced back together. Laboratories can now fire it again.
items.funZh: 2000 年代之后的红外成像研究发现，埃及蓝在红外光下会强烈发光。于是它有了新工作：研究者用它去找那些肉眼已经褪掉的古迹彩绘 —— 帕特农神庙的雕饰、罗马图拉真广场的残件上，靠这点余晖找回了看不见的纹样。一个三千年前的颜料，成了现在的检测工具。
items.funEn: Infrared imaging work since the 2000s found that Egyptian blue luminesces strongly under infrared light, which gave the pigment a new job: researchers use it to recover decoration that has faded beyond the visible. On the sculptures of the Parthenon and fragments from Trajan's Forum in Rome, that faint glow has revealed patterns no eye can see. A pigment three thousand years old now works as a detection tool.

items.aliasZh: 朱砂 · 辰砂 · 丹砂 · 中国「朱」色的来源
items.histZh: 硫化汞。天然产出的叫辰砂，加热汞与硫也能人工合成。它是古代世界最鲜明的一种红：中国人拿它做漆器、印泥、颜料，也拿它炼丹；罗马人在凯旋式上给胜利者涂红脸，用的也是它。因为太醒目，它几乎在所有文明里都被安排在最重要的位置 —— 朱批、朱门、朱印、朱笔。代价是汞：长期接触的工匠会掉发、手抖、性情大变。
items.histEn: Mercury sulfide, found naturally as cinnabar and also made by heating mercury with sulfur. It was the most brilliant red the ancient world had. The Chinese used it for lacquer, seal paste and painting, and also for alchemy; Romans painted the face of a triumphing general with it. Precisely because it shouts, nearly every civilisation put it in the most important place: imperial rescripts, red gates, seal ink, the marking brush. The price was mercury. Workers exposed to it over years lost their hair, developed tremors and changed in temper.
items.funZh: 中国的炼金术士长期相信朱砂里藏着长生与黄金的秘密。加热朱砂会析出水银，水银再与硫反应又变回朱砂，这个循环被读成「死而复生」。秦始皇陵里灌了大量水银，历代方士炼的丹多数含汞，唐代有几位皇帝的死与丹药有关。朱砂在道教里因此同时是仙药和毒物。
items.funEn: Chinese alchemists long believed cinnabar held the secret of immortality and of gold. Heat it and mercury comes off; let the mercury meet sulfur again and it returns to cinnabar. That cycle was read as death and rebirth. Qin Shi Huang's tomb was filled with mercury, the elixirs of later centuries were mostly mercury compounds, and several Tang emperors died in ways their courts connected to those pills. In Daoist practice cinnabar was at once the medicine of immortality and the poison.

items.aliasZh: 铅白 · 白铅 · 雪花白 · 最古老的人造白色
items.aliasEn: Lead white · flake white · the oldest manufactured white
items.histZh: 做法古老得离谱：把铅片挂在醋罐上方，让醋蒸气腐蚀铅，再刮下生成的白色粉末。它遮盖力强、干得快、和油调在一起很顺手，从古希腊到二十世纪的油画几乎每一幅都有一层铅白，不是打底就是提亮。欧洲人把它用在脸上的劲头比用在画布上更狠 —— 伊丽莎白一世用铅白和醋调成的粉涂满面孔和脖颈，因为白就是贵。
items.histEn: The method is startlingly old: hang strips of lead over a pot of vinegar, let the fumes corrode the metal, and scrape off the white powder that forms. It covers well, dries fast and behaves beautifully in oil, so from ancient Greece to the twentieth century nearly every oil painting has lead white somewhere, as ground or as highlight. Europeans were even harder on it as cosmetics. Elizabeth I covered her face and neck with a preparation of lead white and vinegar, because to be white was to be wealthy.
items.funZh: 代价是铅。画家和粉刷匠手抖、腹痛，牙龈上出现一条蓝线；长期涂脸的贵族在慢性中毒。二十世纪它被钛白和锌白取代，但铅白的化学性质也救了它自己：它变黑是因为生成硫化铅，用过氧化氢处理可以变回白色 —— 所以有些被熏黑的古画确实被「洗」回来过。
items.funEn: The price was lead. Painters and decorators got tremors and stomach pain and a blue line along the gums; aristocrats who wore it daily were poisoned slowly. Titanium and zinc white replaced it in the twentieth century, but lead white's chemistry also rescued it: it darkens into lead sulfide, and peroxide treatment can turn it back to white, so some blackened old paintings really were cleaned back to brightness.

items.swZh: 胭脂虫 · 一磅七万只
items.aliasZh: 胭脂红 · 胭脂虫红 · 洋红 · 今天仍在用的天然色素
items.aliasEn: Carmine · cochineal red · still in use today
items.histZh: 从胭脂虫（一种寄生在仙人掌上的介壳虫）体内提取：晒干、碾碎，用酸或水把红浸出来。常被引用的数字是每磅染料约需七万只虫。阿兹特克人早就在用它，西班牙人征服墨西哥后把它做成了大生意，垄断近三百年，它一度是仅次于白银的出口品。欧洲画家的红 —— 从提香到透纳 —— 相当一部分出自这种虫。
items.histEn: It comes from the cochineal, a scale insect that lives on cactus: dry the insects, crush them, and leach the red out with acid or water. The figure usually quoted is some seventy thousand insects to the pound of dye. The Aztecs used it long before the Spanish arrived, and after the conquest Spain turned it into a major trade, holding a near-monopoly for about three centuries; at one point it was second only to silver among exports. Much of the red in European painting, from Titian to Turner, came out of that insect.
items.funZh: 它到现在还活着，只是换了个身份：E120。红色糖果、草莓味酸奶、口红、部分火腿里都可能吃到它。因为「虫」这个词不好听，标签上一般只写「胭脂红」或 E120，于是素食者和某些宗教群体专门去背这份清单。
items.funEn: It is still very much in production, under a new name: E120. You may be eating it in red sweets, strawberry yoghurt, lipstick and some ham. Since the word insect does not sell, labels say carmine or E120 instead, which is why vegetarians and some religious communities keep their own lists to check.

items.aliasZh: 木乃伊棕 · 由木乃伊遗骸磨成的暖棕
items.aliasEn: Mummy brown · a warm brown ground from mummies
items.histZh: 十六世纪起，欧洲的颜料行会把埃及木乃伊连同防腐用的沥青、没药一起磨成粉，做成一种透明的暖棕，用来罩染阴影和肤色。它是从药房流进画室的 —— 木乃伊本来就是欧洲药典里的一味药，从癫痫到胃病都开。拿破仑远征埃及之后欧洲掀起埃及热，木乃伊大量流入，一部分进了客厅，一部分进了调色盘。
items.histEn: From the sixteenth century European colourmen ground Egyptian mummies, together with the bitumen and myrrh used in embalming, into a transparent warm brown for glazes, shadows and flesh tones. It reached the studio by way of the pharmacy: mummy was already a medicine in the European pharmacopoeia, prescribed for everything from epilepsy to stomach complaints. After Napoleon's Egyptian campaign set off a craze, mummies poured into Europe, some into drawing rooms and some onto palettes.
items.funZh: 前拉斐尔派的伯恩-琼斯听说这颜料真的是木乃伊做的之后，立刻跑回画室拿出仅有的一管，在自家花园里给它办了一场正式的葬礼，还插了一株雏菊做标记 —— 当时在场的有他年幼的外甥、后来的作家吉卜林。这种颜料一直生产到二十世纪，1964 年厂商表示木乃伊用完了，才停下。
items.funEn: When the Pre-Raphaelite Edward Burne-Jones learned what the pigment really was, he hurried to his studio, came back with the only tube he owned, and insisted on giving it a decent burial in the garden, with a daisy planted to mark the spot. Among those watching was his young nephew, the future writer Rudyard Kipling. Production continued into the twentieth century; in 1964 the manufacturer reported it had run out of mummies and stopped.

items.aliasZh: 印度黄 · 牛黄 · euxanthin · 颜料史上最著名的悬案
items.aliasEn: Indian yellow · euxanthin · the great pigment mystery
items.histZh: 十七世纪起从印度输入欧洲，是一种透明、带一点荧光的暖黄，透纳和十九世纪风景画家很爱用。长期流传的说法是：用只喂芒果叶的牛，取它的尿，熬干成饼。1883 年的一份报告把它写成虐待动物的产物，1908 年印度禁止了这个做法，颜料随之断供，欧洲画家只好改用别的黄。
items.histEn: Imported from India from the seventeenth century onward, it was a transparent, faintly glowing warm yellow that Turner and the nineteenth-century landscape painters loved. The story long told is that it was made from the urine of cows fed exclusively on mango leaves, boiled down into cakes. An 1883 report described the practice as cruelty to animals, India banned it in 1908, and the supply stopped; European painters switched to other yellows.
items.funZh: 这个故事后来被质疑。有研究者去印度实地调查，找不到这种做法的证据，认为它更可能来自植物；也有人指出当年那份报告本身就是孤证。于是印度黄成了颜料史上最著名的一桩悬案：全世界的资料都在复述同一个故事，但没有人能证明它。
items.funEn: The story has since been questioned. Researchers who went looking in India found no evidence of the practice and argued the pigment more likely came from plants; others point out that the 1883 report stands alone. So Indian yellow became the most famous open case in pigment history: every reference book repeats the same story, and none of them can prove it.

items.aliasZh: 普鲁士蓝 · 柏林蓝 · 铁蓝 · 第一个现代合成颜料
items.aliasEn: Prussian blue · Berlin blue · iron blue
items.histZh: 1706 年前后，在柏林的颜料工迪斯巴赫做红色颜料时，原料被含血的动物性杂质污染，结果沉出一片意料之外的深蓝。他把它卖了出去，配方随后传开 —— 这是第一个既不是从矿物、也不是从植物里来，而是被人做出来的稳定颜料：便宜、耐光、着色力强。它先是改变了绘画，后来又改变了别的：以铁盐感光的「蓝图」成了工程图纸的代称，那条蓝线一直用到现在。
items.histEn: Around 1706 in Berlin, the colourmaker Johann Jacob Diesbach was working up a red when his materials were contaminated with an animal substance containing blood, and an unexpected deep blue precipitated out. He sold it, the recipe spread, and it became the first stable pigment that came neither from a mineral nor a plant but from a workshop: cheap, lightfast and strong. It changed painting first and other things later. Iron-based blueprinting gave engineering drawings their name, and that blue line is still in use.
items.funZh: 浮世绘的蓝也是它。葛饰北斋画《神奈川冲浪里》用的普鲁士蓝，是当时刚经由长崎进入日本的进口颜料；因为它便宜又不易褪色，浮世绘才第一次能画出一整片有层次的天空与海。它还有第二种身份：在医学上，普鲁士蓝是铊中毒和放射性铯中毒的解毒剂，靠它在肠道里把金属离子锁住带走。
items.funEn: It is also the blue of ukiyo-e. When Hokusai made The Great Wave off Kanagawa he was using Prussian blue, an import that had only recently reached Japan through Nagasaki; cheap and hard to fade, it let woodblock prints show a sky and sea with real depth for the first time. The same compound has a second career in medicine, where it is the antidote for thallium and radioactive caesium poisoning, trapping the metal ions in the gut so they can be carried out.

items.aliasZh: 巴黎绿 · 舍勒绿 · 翡翠绿 · 施韦因富特绿
items.aliasEn: Paris green · Scheele's green · emerald green
items.histZh: 1775 年舍勒做出一种含砷的绿色（亚砷酸铜），颜色明亮、成本低，于是十九世纪从画布一路用到了窗帘、壁纸、地毯、女工做的假花和糖果的包装纸。毒性当时就被察觉：潮湿空气会让它释放出含砷的气体，先是房间里的人不舒服，然后是在这种环境下做工的人成批出问题。
items.histEn: In 1775 Carl Wilhelm Scheele produced an arsenic-based green, copper arsenite. It was bright and cheap, and across the nineteenth century it spread from canvas to curtains, wallpaper, carpets, the artificial flowers made by factory women and the wrappers of sweets. Its toxicity was noticed early: damp air made it give off arsenic-bearing vapour, and it was the people in the room, then the people who worked with it, who fell ill first.
items.funZh: 流传最广的一段是拿破仑。圣赫勒拿岛上他住的房间壁纸是绿的，有研究认为潮湿环境会让壁纸里的砷慢慢挥发，长期暴露加剧了他的病情；不过后来对头发的检测显示砷的来源可能不止一处，所以这至今只是假说。真正让它退场的不是故事而是账本：维多利亚时代病历里那些「说不清原因」的皮肤溃疡和神经症状，一条条都指向同一批颜料。
items.funEn: The most repeated episode concerns Napoleon. The wallpaper in his rooms on Saint Helena was green, and one study argued that damp conditions released arsenic from it, worsening his decline; later hair analysis suggested more than one source of arsenic, so the claim remains a hypothesis. What actually retired the pigment was not a story but the records: the unexplained skin ulcers and neurological symptoms scattered through Victorian case notes kept pointing back to the same batch of colour.

items.aliasZh: 雌黄 · 石黄 · 硫化砷 · 与雄黄共生
items.aliasEn: Orpiment · arsenic sulfide · found with realgar
items.histZh: 硫化砷，天然呈柠檬黄到金黄的片状结晶，古代从罗马到中国都在用。它鲜艳、透明，但有毒，而且和含铅的颜料放在一起会互相作用变黑，所以画家用得非常小心，多半只画局部，或者只在纸上用。在中国它还有一个正经用途：纸是黄的，写错字时涂一点雌黄盖住，重新写。
items.histEn: Arsenic sulfide, found naturally as flaky crystals from lemon to golden yellow, used from Rome to China. It is vivid and transparent but poisonous, and it reacts with lead-based colours to turn black, so painters used it sparingly, in isolated passages or on paper. In China it had a second, thoroughly practical use: paper was yellow, and a dab of orpiment covered a mistake so it could be written over.
items.funZh: 「信口雌黄」就是这么来的 —— 古人用雌黄涂改黄纸上的错字，涂掉再写；于是「随口改写事实」被说成信口雌黄。同一个字还有别的用法：「妄下雌黄」指乱改别人的文字。一种有毒的黄色矿物，最后在汉语里变成了「随便乱说」的代名词。
items.funEn: Which is where the Chinese idiom xin kou ci huang comes from: to correct a character on yellow paper you painted orpiment over it and wrote again, so speaking and rewriting the facts at will became the same phrase. A poisonous yellow mineral ended up in the language as shorthand for talking nonsense.

items.aliasZh: 绿土 · 维罗纳绿 · 波希米亚绿 · 灰头土脸的橄榄绿
items.aliasEn: Terre verte · Verona green · green earth
items.histZh: 一种含铁、镁、铝的硅酸盐矿土，磨开是灰扑扑的橄榄绿。它颜色弱、遮盖力低 —— 正因为弱，它成了欧洲绘画里最有用的颜色之一。中世纪和文艺复兴的画家先用它铺一层浅绿的底，再在上面叠加粉红与肉色画脸；底下那层绿压得住红，肤色才透亮而不发灰。
items.histEn: A silicate earth containing iron, magnesium and aluminium; ground up it is a dusty olive green. It is weak in tint and low in opacity, and precisely because it is weak it became one of the most useful colours in European painting. Medieval and Renaissance painters laid a pale green ground first, then built pinks and flesh tones on top; the green beneath holds the red back so the skin stays luminous instead of going grey.
items.funZh: 它也是「中间色」这套技术的代表：画家不直接调出想要的肤色，而是让底色和上层颜色在观看者的眼睛里混合 —— 所以看老画要站远一点，颜色才「合成」。在今天的修复室里，绿土反而好认：它在红外和紫外下的表现很特别，常被用来判断一幅画的底稿改到哪里、有没有被后人动过。
items.funEn: It also stands for the technique of the middle tone: painters did not mix the flesh colour they wanted but let the ground and the layers above it combine inside the viewer's eye, which is why old paintings need a step or two of distance before the colour merges. In conservation labs green earth is easy to identify by its unusual behaviour under infrared and ultraviolet, so it is often used to work out how far an underdrawing was changed and whether later hands touched the picture.

items.aliasZh: 铬黄 · 铅铬黄 · 十九世纪最亮的黄
items.histZh: 十九世纪初从铬矿里做出来的亮黄，成本低、着色力强。梵高在法国南部的阿尔勒用它画向日葵、麦田和那幢黄房子，在给弟弟的信里说自己没有铬黄就没法工作。但铬黄遇光、遇硫化物会变暗变褐 —— 那些向日葵正在慢慢往橄榄色走，它们早就不如一百多年前刚挂上墙时那么亮了。
items.histEn: A bright yellow made from chromium ore in the early nineteenth century, cheap and strong in tint. In Arles, Van Gogh used it for the sunflowers, the wheat fields and the yellow house, and wrote to his brother that he could not work without it. But chrome yellow darkens and browns under light and in the presence of sulfur compounds. The sunflowers are drifting toward olive, and they are no longer anything like as bright as they were the day they were hung.
items.funZh: 尴尬的地方在于它含铅和铬，有毒，而「变暗」又让美术馆两头为难：大规模干预会动到原画的笔触，不动就眼看着它黄下去。几家博物馆都有研究项目，试着在极小的尺度上弄清这层黄到底是怎么变的，但到现在也没有稳妥的复原办法。
items.funEn: The awkward part is that it contains lead and chromium, so it is toxic, and that its darkening leaves museums stuck: intervening on a large scale would disturb the brushwork, and doing nothing means watching it go brown. Several museums run research projects trying to understand at the scale of a few molecules how the yellow changes, but there is still no safe way to put it back.

items.aliasZh: 茜草红 · 茜素色淀 · 又名玫瑰红
items.aliasEn: Madder lake · alizarin lake · rose madder
items.histZh: 茜草根染红的历史可以追到古埃及和罗马，庞贝的壁画里就有用它画的红。但中世纪做绘画颜料走的是另一条路：把根捣碎、发酵，再用明矾把色素沉淀下来做成「色淀」（lake）—— 这样得到的红比直接拿根去染更透明，更适合罩染。在很长一段时间里，它是欧洲画家买得起的那种红。
items.histEn: Madder root dyed red as far back as ancient Egypt and Rome; the wall paintings of Pompeii include it. As a painter's material, though, the medieval route was different: crush the root, let it ferment, then precipitate the colour onto alum to make a lake. The result was more transparent than a straight root dye and better suited to glazing. For centuries it was the red a European painter could actually afford.
items.funZh: 真正能染红的成分在干根里只占百分之一二，剩下全是没用的纤维 —— 想染一匹布，往往要用掉接近布重的根。1868 年茜素被人工合成，天然茜草几乎一夜之间没人要了；有记载说法国南部不少种茜草的田地改种了葡萄。
items.funEn: Only one or two per cent of a dried root is the red itself; the rest is dead weight, so dyeing a single bolt of cloth could take a weight of roots approaching the weight of the cloth. When alizarin was synthesised in 1868, natural madder collapsed almost overnight, and some madder fields in southern France are on record as having been replanted with vines.

items.aliasZh: 那不勒斯黄 · 锑酸铅 · 又名拿浦黄
items.histZh: 名字指向那不勒斯，但更早的配方出现在 17 世纪意大利别处。它的成分是锑酸铅 —— 一种同时含铅和含锑的化合物，毒性不低。好处是遮盖力强、比铬黄耐光，所以从 18 世纪起成了欧洲画亮黄的常用选择。
items.histEn: The name points to Naples, though earlier recipes come from elsewhere in 17th-century Italy. Chemically it is lead antimonate — lead and antimony in one compound, and not a harmless one. Its virtues were opacity and better lightfastness than chrome yellow, which made it a standard bright yellow in European painting from the 18th century on.
items.funZh: 因为含铅，它和附近含硫的颜料会慢慢起反应变黑。修复师在古画上常见到一种斑：原本明黄的地方成了褐色，往往就是两个颜料在几十年里打了架。旧配方还要经过一道煅烧，烟很毒，做颜料的人是最先受害的。
items.funEn: Being a lead pigment, it darkens where sulphur-bearing colours sit nearby. Conservators regularly find patches where a bright yellow has gone brown — two pigments arguing for decades. Old recipes also required a firing step whose fumes were poisonous, and the people making the pigment paid for it first.

items.aliasZh: 天蓝 · 钴玻璃蓝 · 16 世纪起
items.aliasEn: Smalt · cobalt glass blue · from the 16th century
items.histZh: 做法是先把钴矿石磨碎，和石英砂、钾碱一起熔成深蓝的钴玻璃，再把玻璃磨成粉。它从 16 世纪起是欧洲最便宜的蓝，主要去处是替代群青去铺大面积的天空和衣袍。它还有个实际的好处：耐光、不怕碱，所以油画和水性颜料里都能用，不像许多植物染料一见光就退。缺点也很清楚 —— 本身没什么遮盖力，画天空得涂得厚，而涂厚了又容易吸油、显得发暗。
items.histEn: Cobalt ore was ground, melted with quartz sand and potash into a deep blue glass, and the glass then milled to powder. From the 16th century on this was the cheapest blue in Europe — what you used for a large sky or a robe when ultramarine was out of reach. It had a practical virtue too: lightfast and unfazed by alkali, so it worked in oil and in water-based paints alike, unlike many plant dyes. Its weakness is equally clear — it barely covers, so skies went on thick, and thick smalt soaks up oil and darkens.
items.funZh: 它是玻璃，所以磨得越细颜色越淡，越粗才越蓝；更麻烦的是那些极细的粉末会随时间长水解，蓝会慢慢褪成灰绿。伦勃朗《夜巡》里天空发绿，除了清漆泛黄，有研究认为也有它变色的份。它还得按粗细分级卖：最粗的最贵也最蓝，最细的几乎只剩灰白，画家买它跟买砂子一样得挑目数。等到十九世纪合成群青做出来，这种要磨玻璃的蓝就再没人愿意碰了。
items.funEn: Because it is glass, the finer you grind it the paler it gets — coarse grains carry the blue. Worse, the finest dust slowly hydrolyses, and the blue drifts toward grey-green. The greenish sky in Rembrandt's Night Watch has been attributed partly to varnish yellowing and partly, some studies argue, to changes in smalt itself. It was sold graded by grit: the coarsest was dearest and bluest, the finest barely more than grey-white, and a painter bought it the way one buys sand, by mesh. Once synthetic ultramarine appeared in the nineteenth century, nobody bothered grinding glass for blue any more.

items.aliasZh: 铜锈 · 铜绿 · 中世纪抄本常用
items.aliasEn: Verdigris · copper green · common in manuscripts
items.histZh: 做法很直白：把铜片挂在醋上，或者埋进发酵完的葡萄渣里，让表面长出绿色的锈，刮下来拌成颜料。古希腊罗马都这么做，中世纪抄本的画师也用它画叶子。成品不是单一物质，而是醋酸铜和几种碱式醋酸铜的混合物，所以不同批次的颜色能从偏蓝的青绿一直跑到偏黄的草绿。要蓝一点就少让它接触空气，要黄一点就让它多暴露一阵。
items.histEn: The recipe is blunt: hang copper strips over vinegar, or bury them in grape pomace, and scrape off the green corrosion that grows. Greek and Roman painters did it, and so did the illuminators of medieval manuscripts for their leaves. What you end up with is not one compound but a mixture of copper acetates, so batches range from a blue-leaning green to a yellow one. Less air gives the bluer end, a longer exposure the yellower.
items.funZh: 这东西活性极强，会腐蚀纸张和羊皮纸 —— 中世纪抄本里画了绿叶子那几页，常常被自己的颜料咬出洞。它还不肯直接拌油，得先用酒或者尿（靠氨）调过才行。它的英文名来自古法语 vert-de-Grèce，直译是「希腊的绿」——中世纪欧洲人认定最好的铜绿出自希腊。做法却一点也不风雅：把铜片吊在醋缸上方，等醋汽慢慢啃出一层绿霜，再刮下来。
items.funEn: It is chemically aggressive and eats paper and parchment, so green leaves in medieval manuscripts are often ringed by holes burned by their own paint. It also refuses to mix with oil until treated with wine or urine — the ammonia being the point. The English word comes from the Old French vert-de-Grèce, literally "the green of Greece", because medieval Europe believed the finest verdigris came from there. Making it was anything but refined: copper strips were hung over a vat of vinegar and left until the fumes had eaten a green crust out of the metal, which was then scraped off.

items.aliasZh: 死头褐 · 紫褐 · 茜草色淀的副产品
items.aliasEn: Caput mortuum · madder residue · a purple-brown
items.histZh: 拉丁语 caput mortuum 直译是「死人头」，炼金术里指蒸馏之后剩下的渣。作为颜料名，它指茜草色淀提净红色之后沉在底下的那部分 —— 暗红带紫。因为便宜，多用来画衣褶和暗部。它的名字后来被挪用到别的铁红颜料上 —— 今天叫 Caput Mortuum 的基本都是人工铁氧化物，颜色比茜草渣的那一版更靠紫，两条来路不同、名字相同的产品在色卡上其实已经并成了一条。
items.histEn: Caput mortuum means dead head in Latin — in alchemy, the residue left after distillation. As a pigment name it refers to what settled at the bottom once the red had been drawn off a madder lake: a dark, purplish red. Being cheap, it went into shadowed folds and drapery. The name later migrated onto other iron reds; nearly everything sold as Caput Mortuum now is synthetic iron oxide, sitting further toward purple than the madder residue ever did. Two different histories under one name have quietly merged on the colour chart.
items.funZh: 名字吓人，成分其实很温和，除了画画还被拿去当抛光粉，磨金属和宝石。用在皮肤上要小心：它偏紫，涂多了像淤青。这颜色在纸和羊皮纸上是安全的，但它的深紫很容易读成淤青或凝血，所以画人物时几乎只往阴影里放，不往面部放。
items.funEn: Despite the name it is mild stuff, and has also been sold as a polishing powder for metals and gems. On skin it needs care: the purple leans bruise-ward quickly. On paper and parchment it is safe, but the purple depth reads easily as bruising, so on a figure it almost never goes on a face — only into a shadow.

items.aliasZh: 凡戴克棕 · 深棕 · 因画家凡戴克得名
items.aliasEn: Van Dyke brown · named for the painter
items.histZh: 因 17 世纪佛兰德斯的画家凡戴克常用而得名。深、透明、不抢戏，适合做油画的底色层和最后的罩染。它属于所谓的沥青棕一系 —— 原料是泥炭或褐煤，是少数有机来源的棕颜料。这一系的共同问题是干得慢、成膜之后还会继续收缩，所以画得很厚的地方几十年后可能出现细密的龟裂。
items.histEn: Named after the 17th-century Flemish painter Van Dyck, who used it heavily. Dark, transparent, unobtrusive — good for an underpainting and for final glazes. It belongs to the bituminous family, made from peat or lignite, one of the few browns of organic origin. The whole family shares a problem: it dries slowly and keeps shrinking after it sets, so thick passages can craze decades later.
items.funZh: 这类深棕常和另一种叫「沥青」的棕混淆。沥青是溶在松节油里的柏油，几乎永远不干，几十年后会在画上塌出皱纹，把上面的颜料一起拖走。真正的凡戴克棕是安全的土色，只是替沥青背了骂名。
items.funEn: Browns like this get confused with bitumen, which is tar dissolved in turpentine and effectively never dries — decades later it sags, wrinkles, and drags the paint above it out of shape. True Van Dyke brown is tame earth; it just inherits bitumen's reputation.

items.aliasZh: 生赭 · 锡耶纳土 · 含水的氧化铁
items.aliasEn: Raw sienna · terre de sienne · iron oxide with water
items.histZh: 意大利锡耶纳城附近产的土，氧化铁里还带着水，颜色是偏黄的棕。锡耶纳这个地名本身就成了「土色」的代称。锡耶纳土在文艺复兴时期是标准的地色颜料 —— 便宜、稳定、干得快，常被用来整面铺底，再往上叠别的颜色。今天还叫这个名字的颜料里，天然矿和合成氧化铁都有，色相基本一致。
items.histEn: Earth dug near the Italian city of Siena, iron oxide with water still bound into it — a yellowish brown. The place name itself became a word for the colour. Siena earth became a standard ground in the Renaissance: cheap, stable, quick drying, laid across a whole panel before anything went on top. What carries the name today may be dug or synthesised iron oxide; the hue is much the same either way.
items.funZh: 把它烧一下，水跑掉，就变成红棕色的「熟赭」。也就是说生赭和熟赭是同一种矿的两种状态 —— 有一管生赭和一只炉子，就能自己做熟赭。它也常被画油画的人用来垫暖 —— 在冷色底下先铺一层薄薄的生赭，上面再罩蓝或紫，颜色会显得通透而不是发闷。这是很老的一招，但至今管用。
items.funEn: Fire it and the water leaves, and the yellowish brown turns into the reddish brown called burnt sienna. Raw and burnt sienna are one earth in two states — a tin of raw sienna and a flame are all it takes. Oil painters also use it to warm a ground: a thin raw sienna under cool colours, with blue or violet glazed over it, keeps the result transparent instead of dead. An old trick that still works.

items.aliasZh: 熟褐 · 烧棕土 · 干得极快
items.aliasEn: Burnt umber · fired brown earth · dries fast
items.histZh: umber 来自意大利语 terra d'ombra，「翁布里亚的土」，那里产含锰和铁的棕土。原土是灰绿的（也就是生褐），煅烧之后锰被氧化，转成深褐。它干得极快，所以成了油画里最常用的速干底色。土色系的颜料不怕混、也不挑媒介，从壁画到油画一直没被淘汰。今天的熟褐多半已经是人工合成的铁氧化物，色号和几百年前取的那块土不同，但那种偏冷的深棕还是照着老样子在调。
items.histEn: Umber comes from terra d'ombra, earth of Umbria, where the brown soil carries both manganese and iron. Raw, it is grey-green; fired, the manganese oxidises and it turns a deep warm brown. It dries unusually fast, which is why it became the standard quick-drying underpainting brown in oils. Earth colours tolerate mixing and take any medium, which is why they survived the trip from fresco to oil paint. Most burnt umber today is synthetic iron oxide: a different colour number from the lump dug up centuries ago, with the cool depth still mixed to match.
items.funZh: 生褐和熟褐是同一块土的两种状态，用起来却是两回事：生褐偏冷，管阴影里的青；熟褐偏暖，管阴影里的焦。画室里有句说法 —— 生褐让人脸发绿、熟褐让人脸发黑，两个都别直接往脸上抹。
items.funEn: Raw and burnt are the same earth but behave like opposites: raw is cool, for the blue inside a shadow; burnt is warm, for the scorch. Studio lore puts it bluntly — raw umber turns a face green, burnt umber turns it black. Neither wants to be applied neat.

items.aliasZh: 象牙黑 · 骨黑 · 中世纪起
items.aliasEn: Ivory black · bone black · since the Middle Ages
items.histZh: 把象牙或者骨头放进密闭容器里闷烧成炭。中世纪起用于油画，也大量用于印刷油墨和黑色蜡。工艺上的关键是密闭 —— 通着空气烧只能烧成白灰，只有缺氧闷烧才能留下炭黑。磨出来偏暖，比葡萄藤炭黑少一点冷调，所以画阴影和衣服暗部时它更容易和暖色接上。
items.histEn: Ivory or bone burned to charcoal in a sealed vessel. In oil painting since the Middle Ages, and in bulk for printing ink and blacking. The trick is the sealed vessel: with air it burns to white ash, and only a starved fire leaves carbon black. Ground, it reads warm rather than cool, which is why it joins a warm shadow more easily than vine black does.
items.funZh: 如今叫「象牙黑」的，几乎都是骨头做的（bone black），因为象牙买卖早已被禁。颜料名里就这么留着一个买不到的材料 —— 木乃伊棕是真停产了，象牙黑只是换了原料。名字里的象牙其实是个误会：烧的不是象牙本身，而是骨头和象牙的边角料 —— 正经该叫骨黑。烧出来的黑带一点暖棕，不像炭黑那样冷硬，所以画肤色和布料时最讨巧。
items.funEn: Nearly everything sold as ivory black today is bone black, since the ivory trade has long been banned. The name keeps a material you can no longer buy — a cousin of mummy brown, which really did stop being made. The ivory in the name is a misunderstanding. What is burned is not ivory as such but bone and ivory offcuts — bone black, properly speaking. The result is a black with a warm brown undertone, nothing like the cold hardness of carbon black, which is exactly why it suits skin and cloth.

items.aliasZh: 钴蓝 · 铝酸钴 · 泰纳尔 1802
items.histZh: 1820 年代之前，画家想用钴的颜色只有一条路：把它烧成玻璃再磨成粉，也就是 smalt。1802 年泰纳尔在实验室制出一种纯的钴蓝，1820 年代法国开始量产。画家从此第一次有了便宜、稳定、遮盖力又好的蓝。
items.histEn: Before the 1820s the only route to cobalt's colour in paint was to melt it into glass and grind that glass — smalt. In 1802 Thénard made a pure cobalt blue in the laboratory, and by the 1820s France was manufacturing it. Painters had, for the first time, a blue that was cheap, stable and opaque at once.
items.funZh: 印象派把钴蓝用疯了 —— 他们画里那些紫、以及阴影里的蓝，很多是钴蓝调出来的。它的毛病只有一个：贵。是那种要算着往外挤的贵。它还有个身世转弯：中世纪的矿工把那种在炉子里冒烟、既毒人又不肯出金属的矿石叫「kobold」——地精。那东西正是钴。一个原本用来骂矿妖的词，最后成了颜色自己的名字。
items.funEn: The Impressionists went through cobalt blue at a rate — much of their violet, and much of the blue inside a shadow, is cobalt. Its one defect is price, of the kind that makes you count what you squeeze out. There is a twist in its name. Medieval miners called the troublesome ore that fumed in the smelter kobold — goblin — because it poisoned them and refused to give up metal. The ore was cobalt, and the insult eventually became the name of the colour itself.

items.aliasZh: 镉红 · 硒硫化镉 · 镉系的红
items.histZh: 镉是 1817 年在锌矿里被认出来的一种杂质。镉黄先出来（1840 年代），镉红是后来往硫化镉里掺硒做成的，1910 年前后进市场。它偏暖、遮盖力强、耐光，一上市就成了画红的首选。它也是少数比同族颜料晚了很久才出现的颜色 —— 镉黄 1840 年代就上市了，镉红要等到 1910 年前后，因为把硒稳定地掺进晶格这件事花了很长时间。一种颜料什么时候诞生，往往取决于化学上的难点卡在哪里。
items.histEn: Cadmium was identified in 1817 as an impurity in zinc ore. Cadmium yellow came first, in the 1840s; the red followed by adding selenium to the cadmium sulphide, reaching the market around 1910. Warm, opaque and lightfast, it became the default red almost at once. It is also one of the few pigments that arrived long after its own family: cadmium yellow was on the market in the 1840s, while the red had to wait until around 1910, because getting selenium into the lattice stably took decades. When a pigment appears usually depends on where the chemistry is hard.
items.funZh: 镉有毒，这点没有争议 —— 但真正危险的是做颜料的人和用喷笔的人，吸进粉尘最伤肺。画完干透的镉颜料很难再析出来。结论也简单：别磨、别喷、别让谁去啃画。镉在颜料里的第一次露面其实不是红，是黄。1840 年代它先被做成黄颜料，很快成了印象派的常客；等做出红，已经是几十年后的事。同一块金属，黄和红都占了，而且都很扎实。
items.funEn: Cadmium is toxic, no argument — but the people at risk are those making the pigment and those spraying it, breathing dust. Once dry in a film it is very hard to get at. So: don't sand it, don't spray it, don't let anyone chew the painting. Cadmium's first appearance in paint was not red but yellow. From the 1840s it was being made as a yellow pigment and quickly became a favourite of the Impressionists; the red only arrived decades later. The same metal ended up supplying both, and both of them opaque and dependable.

items.aliasZh: 镉黄 · 硫化镉 · 取代铬黄
items.histZh: 1840 年代德国人把硫化镉沉淀出来做成颜料。它的出现让画家可以不用再碰两种麻烦的黄：含铅的铬黄，和含砷的舍勒绿那一类。具体做法是把镉盐和硫化物放进溶液里，让黄色的硫化镉沉下来，再洗掉可溶的盐。深浅靠镉锌比例调：掺锌多偏柠檬黄，纯一点偏橙。它比铬黄贵，但耐光得多，所以在户外和需要长期保存的画上很快占了上风。
items.histEn: In the 1840s German chemists precipitated cadmium sulphide as a pigment. It let painters stop reaching for two troublesome yellows: chrome yellow, which carries lead, and the arsenic-bearing greens of the Scheele's green family. The method was precipitation: cadmium salts meeting a sulphide in solution so the yellow settles out, then washing away the soluble salts. Shade was tuned by the cadmium-to-zinc ratio, more zinc toward lemon, less toward orange. Costlier than chrome yellow and far more lightfast, which is why it took over outdoors and in work meant to last.
items.funZh: 梵高在阿尔勒那段日子特别爱用镉黄，写信跟弟弟提奥要颜料时点过名。他那些亮到发烫的向日葵和黄房子，很大一部分就是靠这一管撑起来的。镉黄也是被替代得最彻底的一批颜料之一 —— 今天在美术用品店买到的「镉黄」，很多是偶氮颜料仿的色调，便宜、无毒，耐光也够用。真要买含镉的，通常得单独订。
items.funEn: Van Gogh leaned on cadmium yellow hard through his Arles period, naming it when he wrote to Theo for supplies. The sunflowers and the yellow house, lit to the point of discomfort, are largely this tube. Cadmium yellows are also among the most thoroughly substituted pigments: much of what a shop sells as cadmium yellow today is an azo hue imitating it — cheaper, non-toxic, lightfast enough. The real thing usually has to be ordered specially.

items.aliasZh: 锌白 · 氧化锌 · 1840 年代起
items.aliasEn: Zinc white · zinc oxide · from the 1840s
items.histZh: 18 世纪末法国人从锌矿里把它做出来，1840 年代开始在油画里站住脚。它比铅白更透明、更冷，而且不会像铅白那样一遇到硫就发黑。更具体的时间点是 1782 年前后，法国化学家居东·德·莫尔沃给出了可行的制法，到 1834 年法国开始工业化生产。所以它比人们印象里现代得多 —— 在它之前，画家手里的白基本只有铅白一种。
items.histEn: Worked out from zinc ore in France at the end of the 18th century, and established in oil painting by the 1840s. It is more transparent and cooler than lead white, and unlike lead white it does not blacken on meeting sulphur. The date usually given is around 1782, when the French chemist Guyton de Morveau published a workable method, with industrial production in France following by 1834. That makes it far more recent than people assume: before it, a painter's white was essentially lead white and nothing else.
items.funZh: 它有个要命的缺点：干后的油膜偏脆，容易裂。所以后来大家改用钛白，锌白降级成往里掺一点点的配角 —— 用来调稠度，不用来盖东西。它在水彩和丙烯里反而活得不错 —— 那两种材料不靠油膜，脆裂的问题根本不存在。所以锌白今天的定位更像「水性的白」，油画里的那份工作则基本被钛白接管了。
items.funEn: Its fatal flaw is a dry film that goes brittle and cracks. Titanium white took over as a result, and zinc white was demoted to a small addition for body rather than a covering white. It does well in watercolour and acrylic, where there is no oil film to go brittle and nothing to crack. That makes its modern role more like the white of water-based media, while oils have largely handed the job to titanium.

items.aliasZh: 钛白 · 二氧化钛 · 现在最常用的白
items.aliasEn: Titanium white · titanium dioxide · the default white
items.histZh: 钛白的实验室记录可以追到 1821 年，但一直到 1916 年挪威才做出能工业化的方法，1919 年才作为颜料上市。它是目前遮盖力最强的白。难点在于钛很难从矿石里提干净，早期产品还会随时间发黄。真正解决问题的是把二氧化钛做成极细的颗粒并量产 —— 这一步同时把它变成了涂料、塑料、造纸工业的基础原料，颜料只是它最小的一个用途。
items.histEn: Titanium white was described in a laboratory as early as 1821, but no industrial route existed until Norway worked one out in 1916; it reached the market as a pigment in 1919. Nothing covers like it. The hard part was extracting titanium cleanly from ore, and early product yellowed with age. What fixed it was making titanium dioxide as extremely fine particles at scale, the same step that turned it into a base material for paints, plastics and paper. Pigment is its smallest use.
items.funZh: 钛白一出来，铅白和锌白在油画里就退到二线了。它也不只待在画上 —— 牙膏、防晒霜、纸、塑料里的白，多半也是它。你今天摸到的白色东西，很可能就是这管颜料。它差点当不上颜料：纯钛白容易吸潮成块，单独盖一层会发脆掉粉。真正让它能画画的关键不是提纯，而是给每颗二氧化钛颗粒包上一层氧化铝或二氧化硅的壳 —— 是包壳的事，不是纯度的事。
items.funEn: Once it arrived, lead white and zinc white retreated in oil painting. Nor does it stay on canvas — the white in toothpaste, sunscreen, paper and plastic is usually the same compound. Most white things you touched today were this pigment. It very nearly never became a paint at all. Pure titanium white is chalking and moisture-hungry, and a film of it alone grows brittle. What made it usable was not purification but packaging: coating each particle of titanium dioxide in a shell of alumina or silica so the pigment could sit in oil without falling apart.

items.aliasZh: 铅锡黄 · 中世纪到 18 世纪
items.histZh: 中世纪到 18 世纪欧洲画家用来画最亮那道黄的颜料，成分是铅和锡一起烧成的氧化物。它比雌黄稳定得多，维米尔、伦勃朗都用得很多。它的配方有两种：一种偏黄（Type I），一种偏黄橙（Type II），后者往往和锡灰一起出现。做法是把铅和锡一起煅烧，温度和配比差一点就烧不出色，所以这是中世纪作坊里的手艺活 —— 也解释了它为什么会在 18 世纪断掉。
items.histEn: The brightest yellow on a European palette from the Middle Ages to the 18th century, made by firing lead and tin into an oxide. Far more stable than orpiment, it was used in quantity by Vermeer and Rembrandt. Two variants exist: the yellower Type I and the orange-leaning Type II, which usually turns up alongside tin ash. Making either meant calcining lead and tin together, and a small error in temperature or ratio gave nothing at all. It was a craftsman's job, which is part of why the knowledge died out in the 18th century.
items.funZh: 这颜色在 18 世纪之后没人会做了，配方失传。而现代分析发现它的老化并不一致 —— 有研究认为其中一种变体会在光下慢慢灰掉，如果真是这样，我们现在看到的那些黄叶子比画家当年画的要暗。
items.funEn: After the 18th century nobody could make it any more; the recipe was lost. Modern analysis finds it did not age uniformly either — some studies argue one variant greys in light, which would mean the yellow leaves we see now are darker than the ones the painter made.

items.aliasZh: 凯米斯红 · 虫红 · 比胭脂虫更早
items.aliasEn: Kermes · insect red · older than cochineal
items.histZh: 用长在圣栎上的一种小介壳虫做的红，地中海地区从古代一直用到中世纪，比美洲的胭脂虫早了上千年。收虫的时机极讲究：要趁雌虫还没产卵、体内色素最满的时候采，采下来晒干或熏死，磨成粉再上媒染剂。同等重量下它的染色力比胭脂虫差得多，所以中世纪要染一件像样的红袍，用掉的虫数以十万计，价格是和黄金放在一起比的。
items.histEn: A red made from a small scale insect that lives on the kermes oak, used around the Mediterranean from antiquity through the Middle Ages — a thousand years before the cochineal of the Americas arrived. Timing mattered: the insects were gathered before the females laid eggs, when the pigment was densest, then dried or fumigated and ground onto a mordant. Weight for weight it dyes far less than cochineal does, so reddening a proper robe in the Middle Ages took insects by the hundred thousand, and the price was quoted against gold.
items.funZh: 英语 crimson、法语 carmin、西班牙语 carmesí、阿拉伯语 qirmiz，都是从这种虫的名字来的，再往上还能追到梵语的 kṛmi，意思是「虫」。好几种语言里「深红」这个词，追到底是「虫色」。
items.funEn: English crimson, French carmin, Spanish carmesí and Arabic qirmiz all descend from the name of this insect, and further back from Sanskrit kṛmi, worm. In several languages the word for deep red is, at root, the word for a bug.

items.aliasZh: 孔雀石 · 孔雀石绿 · 碱式碳酸铜
items.histZh: 天然碱式碳酸铜，磨成粉就是绿颜料，和中国画里「石绿」用的是同一族矿物。古埃及人把它磨进眼影，俄国的圣像画里也大量用它。它和中国画里的石绿几乎是一套做法：先研、再漂、按颗粒分级，最粗的那一级铺底，最细的收尾。颗粒越细颜色越浅，这条规律对铜系的绿颜料全都成立，所以画家手上的一块绿，往往同时有深浅好几档。
items.histEn: Natural basic copper carbonate, ground into a green pigment — the same mineral family behind 石绿 in Chinese painting. Egyptians ground it into eye paint; Russian icon painters used it in quantity. Preparing it is essentially the same as for 石绿 in Chinese painting: grind, levigate, grade by grain size, the coarsest laying in the ground and the finest finishing. Finer grinding always means paler for copper greens, so a painter's stock of green came in several depths at once.
items.funZh: 它和钴玻璃蓝一样有「磨得越细越浅」的毛病，所以画家会把它筛成几个粗细等级分开用。另外它是铜矿露在地表的信号 —— 在山上看见孔雀石，就知道底下有铜。它还是最早被拿来当眼影的矿物之一。古埃及人磨成粉敷在眼周 —— 在那种炎热里，绿色看着比黑色凉。但磨得太细会变浅发灰，所以老手艺要按粗细分层：粗的垫底，细的提亮。
items.funEn: Like smalt, it pales as it is ground finer, so painters sieved it into grades and used them separately. It is also a surface signal for copper ore: malachite on a hillside means copper underneath. It was also among the first minerals used as eye paint. In ancient Egypt it was ground and applied around the eyes — green, in that heat, reads cooler than black. But grinding it too fine lightens and greys it, so the old trade sorted it by grit: coarse for the base, fine for the highlights.

items.aliasZh: 雄黄 · 鸡冠石 · 西方叫 realgar
items.aliasEn: Realgar · ruby sulphur · the same mineral as 雄黄
items.histZh: 西方名 realgar 来自阿拉伯语 rahj al-ghār，「矿洞里的粉」。它是橙红色的砷硫化物，常和黄色的雌黄长在一起。中国的雄黄和西方的 realgar 是同一种矿。它软得出奇 —— 硬度只有 1.5 到 2，指甲就能划出痕，这也是它常被磨成粉入药的原因。做颜料同样要磨，而磨的过程会起粉尘；旧时没人知道砷的事，今天看这是很危险的一道工序。
items.histEn: The Western name comes from Arabic rahj al-ghār, powder of the mine. It is an orange-red arsenic sulphide that commonly grows beside the yellow orpiment. Chinese 雄黄 and Western realgar are the same mineral. It is startlingly soft, 1.5 to 2 on the hardness scale, soft enough for a fingernail, which is part of why it was also ground for medicine. Pigment meant grinding it too, and grinding raises dust. Nobody knew about the arsenic then; by modern standards it is a hazardous step.
items.funZh: 含砷，而且在光下会慢慢分解成雌黄和砒霜那一类东西 —— 越放越黄，也越放越毒。中国端午旧俗要喝雄黄酒、拿它驱虫，按今天的眼光看，那是一条挺危险的习俗。雄黄和雌黄在矿里常长在一起，一个橙红一个柠檬黄，古人把这对矿石合称「鸳鸯矿」。可雄黄见光见热会慢慢变成雌黄 —— 敦煌和古埃及那些橙红的笔触，今天不少已经发黄，是颜色自己在岁月里挪了位。
items.funEn: It contains arsenic and decomposes in light toward orpiment and the arsenic trioxide family — yellower and more poisonous with age. The old Duanwu custom of drinking realgar wine to drive off insects reads, by modern lights, as a fairly dangerous one. In the ground, realgar and orpiment grow side by side — one orange-red, one lemon yellow — and old Chinese sources called the pair the mandarin-duck ores. Realgar, however, slowly turns into orpiment when exposed to light and heat. Many of the orange-red strokes at Dunhuang and in Egyptian work have drifted toward yellow, the colour moving on its own, in its own time.

items.aliasZh: 蓝铜矿 · 石青矿 · 中世纪叫「德国蓝」
items.aliasEn: Azurite · the mineral behind 石青
items.histZh: 另一种天然碱式碳酸铜，这次是蓝的。中世纪欧洲叫它「德国蓝」或「山蓝」，也是中国画里「石青」的原料。用之前要反复研漂：把矿砸碎、加水搅拌，让颗粒按粗细分层沉下去。粗的颗粒颜色最正、最蓝，细的会偏浅偏灰，所以粗的那一级留给最重要的位置，细的才用来画远山 —— 这一步决定它能不能顶替群青。
items.histEn: The other natural basic copper carbonate, and this one is blue — called German blue or mountain blue in medieval Europe, and the source mineral for 石青 in Chinese painting. Before use it was levigated: crushed, stirred in water, and left to settle out in layers by grain size. Coarse grains carry the truest blue and the finest go pale and grey, so the coarse grade went where ultramarine would have gone and the fine grade painted distant hills.
items.funZh: 它和孔雀石是同族矿物，会在潮湿环境里慢慢变成孔雀石 —— 所以有些古画上的蓝袍子今天看着是绿的，不一定是画家画绿的，是自己变的。画家还会按颗粒粗细分级：最粗的垫天空，细的用来画远山。
items.funEn: It belongs to the same family as malachite and slowly converts into it in damp conditions — so some blue robes in old paintings are green today without the painter ever choosing green. Painters also graded it by grain size: coarsest for a sky's base, finest for distant hills.

items.aliasZh: 沥青棕 · 柏油棕 · 19 世纪的灾难
items.histZh: 把天然沥青溶进松节油当棕颜料，18 到 19 世纪流行过一阵，因为它能做出别的棕做不出的那种半透明、温润的效果。它当年的卖点其实很技术：别的棕要靠厚涂才有深度，而沥青溶在松节油里能做成极稀的透明层，一层就出效果。省时间、省颜料，对一个接订单的画室来说这是实打实的诱惑。
items.histEn: Natural bitumen — tar — dissolved in turpentine and used as a brown. It had a vogue in the 18th and 19th centuries because it gave a translucency and depth other browns could not. Its selling point was technical: other browns needed thickness to show depth, whereas bitumen dissolved in turpentine could be laid as an extremely thin transparent film and work in one pass. Less time and less paint, which is a real temptation for a studio working to commission.
items.funZh: 这东西基本从没干过。它不会真正固化，几十年后慢慢流动、塌陷，把盖在它上面的颜料一起拖进皱纹里。19 世纪留下不少「画着画着自己烂掉」的记录，而且修不回来。它最大的毛病是干得没完没了。十九世纪就有人记过：用沥青打底的画过几十年还在往下淌，裂缝、下陷、颜色跟着往里跑，修复师干脆叫它「沥青病」。想用它又不后悔，得先铺一层别的颜料隔开。
items.funEn: It essentially never dries. It does not truly set, and over decades it creeps, sags, and drags the paint above it into wrinkles. The 19th century left a number of documented cases of paintings destroying themselves, beyond repair. Its real problem is that it never finishes drying. Nineteenth-century observers noted that pictures grounded in bitumen were still creeping downward decades later — cracking, sinking, dragging colour with them. Restorers call it bitumen disease. If you want to use it without regret, lay a barrier of something else underneath.

items.histZh: 钴天蓝是钴与锡的氧化物，1860 年前后作为颜料上市，比同时代的合成群青更绿、更稳。它最出名的用处是画天空 —— 印象派画家嫌群青太紫，钴天蓝正好落在他们想要的那个位置上，于是天空和阴影里的蓝大面积换成了它。屏幕上的钴天蓝是近似值，真颜料遮盖力很强。
items.histEn: Cerulean is a cobalt tin oxide that reached the market around 1860, greener and more stable than the synthetic ultramarine of the same period. Its great use was sky. The Impressionists found ultramarine too violet, and cerulean landed exactly where they wanted, so skies and shadow blues were repainted in it wholesale. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is strongly opaque.
items.funZh: 钴天蓝有个别名跟它的成分有关：因为含锡，它在酸里比其他钴颜料更抗咬，画在户外也稳定。代价是含钴的颜料一贯的毛病 —— 贵。莫奈晚年画睡莲系列用了大量钴类颜料，账单一度相当难看。
items.funEn: Cerulean's tin content makes it more resistant to acid than other cobalt pigments and stable outdoors, which is why it survived on exterior work. The price is the usual penalty attached to cobalt: money. Monet's late water-lily series consumed a great deal of cobalt pigment, and the bills were accordingly grim.

items.histZh: 钴紫是磷酸钴，1859 年前后问世，是第一种真正耐光的紫颜料 —— 在此之前，画家手里的紫要么靠红蓝相调、要么用极不稳定的有机染料，都不耐久。钴紫一来就成了稳定紫色的标准答案，莫奈、雷诺阿的花卉里都能找到它。屏幕上的钴紫是近似值，真颜料比这个更灰更闷。
items.histEn: Cobalt violet is a cobalt phosphate, introduced around 1859 and the first genuinely lightfast violet pigment. Before it, a painter's purples came either from mixing red with blue or from organic dyes that faded badly. It arrived as the dependable answer for purple, and it can be found in the flowers of Monet and Renoir. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is greyer and flatter.
items.funZh: 钴紫有个不太被提起的特点：它极透明，罩染时几乎像一层有色玻璃，所以在古典技法里常用来做最后的透明罩染，而不用来堆厚。透明度高的颜料遮盖力差，但改色能力极强，这是二选一。
items.funEn: Cobalt violet is markedly transparent, glazing almost like a sheet of tinted glass, which is why classical technique reserved it for final transparent glazes rather than building it up thickly. Highly transparent pigments cover poorly and modify colour superbly, and you cannot have both.

items.histZh: 钴绿是锌与钴的氧化物，1780 年由瑞典化学家林曼制得，所以又叫林曼绿。它比巴黎绿那种含砷的绿安全得多，颜色却偏灰、着色力弱，所以一直没成为主流。它的意义更多在环保史上：在那个绿颜料普遍含铜含砷的年代，它提供了一个无毒的选项。屏幕上的钴绿是近似值，真颜料比这个淡不少。
items.histEn: Cobalt green is a zinc cobalt oxide prepared by the Swedish chemist Rinman in 1780, and it still carries his name. Far safer than the arsenic-bearing greens such as Paris green, it is also greyer and weaker in tinting strength, which kept it out of the mainstream. Its real importance is in the history of safety: at a time when greens were routinely full of copper and arsenic, it offered a non-toxic option.
items.funZh: 钴绿着色力弱的毛病在实用上很尴尬：想要浓就得堆很多，堆多又显得脏。所以它常常不是主色，而是用来「压」别的绿 —— 在鲜艳的绿里加一点钴绿，能把颜色往灰里拉，同时不损失耐光性。
items.funEn: Weak tinting strength is awkward in practice: to get depth you need a great deal of it, and too much of it reads muddy. So it tends to serve as a moderating colour rather than a principal one — a little cobalt green added to a vivid green pulls it toward grey without costing any lightfastness.

items.histZh: 锰紫是磷酸锰铵，1868 年在德国取得专利，所以又叫纽伦堡紫。它比钴紫便宜、比有机紫稳定，成了 19 世纪末紫色颜料的另一个选项。它的色相比钴紫更红更暖，接近洋红。屏幕上的锰紫是近似值，真颜料偏哑光，堆厚会显得干。
items.histEn: Manganese violet is a manganese ammonium phosphate, patented in Germany in 1868 and hence also called Nuremberg violet. Cheaper than cobalt violet and far more stable than the organic violets, it became a second option for purple at the end of the nineteenth century. Its hue runs redder and warmer than cobalt violet, edging toward magenta. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is matte and looks dry when applied thickly.
items.funZh: 锰紫是少数几种「不含重金属毒」的紫：锰本身是人体微量元素，虽然吸入粉尘仍有害，但比含铅含镉的颜料安全得多。所以它在 20 世纪的颜料安全改造里留了下来，至今仍在产。
items.funEn: Manganese violet is one of the few purples free of the classic heavy-metal poisons. Manganese is a trace element the body needs, and while inhaling the dust is still harmful it is far safer than lead- or cadmium-bearing pigments, which is why it survived the twentieth-century reformulation of artists' materials and is still made.

items.histZh: 锰蓝是锰酸钡，1935 年才作为颜料上市，是这份色卡里最年轻的一批之一。它的蓝介于青和天蓝之间，比酞菁蓝更清、更绿。因为生产过程中要处理钡盐、废水难处理，它在 1990 年代基本停产，如今市面上卖的多数是替代品。屏幕上的锰蓝按停产前的原品取色。
items.histEn: Manganese blue is barium manganate, first sold as a pigment in 1935 and among the youngest entries on this card. Its blue sits between cyan and sky, clearer and greener than phthalo. Because production involves barium salts and difficult wastewater, it was largely discontinued in the 1990s, and most of what is sold today is a substitute. This sample follows the original before it went out of production.
items.funZh: 因为停产，锰蓝成了颜料收藏圈里的一个话题：老库存的管装颜料价格一路上涨，有人专门收集停产色。这也带来一个实际问题 —— 修复一幅用了真锰蓝的画，今天很难找到成分一致的补色材料。
items.funEn: Being discontinued made manganese blue a topic in pigment collecting: old tubes of it climb in price, and there are people who specialise in out-of-production colours. It also creates a practical problem, in that restoring a painting that used genuine manganese blue means finding a matching material that no longer exists.

items.histZh: 酞菁蓝是铜酞菁，1935 年由英国的染料工业偶然做出来，随后进入颜料领域。它一上市就把蓝颜料的价格打了下来 —— 着色力极强，一点就能顶很多，而且耐光耐酸碱几乎无懈可击。代价是它太强力、太干净，混色时极容易一口吃掉别人。屏幕上的酞菁蓝是近似值。
items.histEn: Phthalo blue is copper phthalocyanine, stumbled on by the British dye industry in 1935 and soon taken up as a pigment. Its arrival collapsed the price of blue: the tinting strength is enormous, a little goes a very long way, and its resistance to light, acid and alkali is close to perfect. The price is that it is too strong and too clean, and in a mixture it will eat whatever it is combined with. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 酞菁蓝有个别名能说明它的性格：有人叫它「暴君蓝」。在调色盘上，只要笔尖上还剩一点点酞菁蓝，去调别的颜色就会把对方全染成蓝 —— 所以用它之后必须彻底洗笔，这在油画圈几乎是一条纪律。
items.funEn: One nickname for it captures the character: tyrant blue. If any trace of phthalo remains on the brush, whatever colour you mix next turns blue — which is why washing the brush thoroughly afterwards amounts to a rule among oil painters.

items.histZh: 酞菁绿是酞菁蓝的氯化版本，结构上只多几个氯原子，颜色却从蓝直接跳到了绿 —— 这是有机颜料里很典型的一个现象：分子上换几个小基团，吸收波长就整体挪位。它同样着色力极强，是现代调绿的主力。屏幕上的酞菁绿是近似值。
items.histEn: Phthalo green is the chlorinated version of phthalo blue. A few extra chlorine atoms on the molecule swing the colour all the way from blue to green — a common behaviour in organic pigments, where small changes to the structure shift the absorption band bodily. It too has enormous tinting strength and is a mainstay of modern green mixing. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 酞菁绿的深色调在纯色时看着几乎发黑，要稀释很多才显出正绿。这个特点让它在老式配方里常被拿来加深色，也导致不少人第一次用它时下手过重 —— 一小点就够，多了整幅画都暗掉。
items.funEn: Undiluted, phthalo green looks nearly black, and it takes a great deal of thinning before a true green appears. That is why older recipes used it for deepening, and why so many people overdo it the first time: a touch is enough, and too much darkens an entire painting.

items.histZh: 汉紫是硅酸铜钡，与汉蓝同族，是中国在战国末至汉代人工合成的颜料，用在陶俑彩绘和墓室壁画上。它比埃及蓝晚、比玛雅蓝早，而且这三个文明各自独立做出了结构相近的合成颜料，在颜料史上很特别。汉代以后这项技术失传，直到现代分析仪器才确认它的成分。屏幕上的汉紫按出土样品取色。
items.histEn: Han purple is a barium copper silicate, related to Han blue and synthesised in China from the late Warring States into the Han period for painted figures and tomb murals. It postdates Egyptian blue and predates Maya blue, and the three civilisations independently produced structurally similar synthetic pigments — a striking fact in the history of pigments. The technique was lost after the Han, and the composition was only confirmed with modern instrumentation. This sample follows excavated material.
items.funZh: 汉紫有个特别之处：它在紫外和红外下会发出很强的荧光，这让考古人员可以在不取样的情况下，用便携设备在现场扫描大型壁画，把用汉紫画过的区域直接标出来 —— 相当于让两千年前的颜色自己举手。
items.funEn: Han purple fluoresces strongly under ultraviolet and infrared, which lets archaeologists scan large murals in situ with portable instruments and map exactly where the pigment was used without taking samples. The colour, in effect, raises its own hand across two thousand years.

items.histZh: 汉蓝同样是硅酸铜钡，与汉紫共用一套制备工艺，只是配比不同。它在中国出现得极早，是已知最早的合成蓝色颜料之一，比埃及蓝稍晚但工艺独立。秦兵马俑上残留的紫蓝色痕迹里就有它。这类颜料需要精确控制原料比例和烧成温度，属于相当高端的古代技术。屏幕上的汉蓝按出土样品取色。
items.histEn: Han blue is the same barium copper silicate as Han purple, produced by a shared process with a different ratio of ingredients. It appears in China remarkably early, among the earliest known synthetic blue pigments — slightly later than Egyptian blue, but arrived at independently. Traces of it survive on the painted terracotta figures of the first emperor. Making it required precise control of both proportions and firing temperature, marking it as a genuinely advanced ancient technology.
items.funZh: 汉蓝和汉紫的合成要先把原料烧到接近 1000 度，再缓慢降温，温度曲线稍微不对就出不了色。所以这两样颜料的出现其实说明当时已经掌握了相当精细的窑温控制 —— 颜料史往往就是材料控制能力的证据。
items.funEn: Making Han blue or purple means firing the ingredients to around a thousand degrees and then cooling slowly; a slightly wrong curve and no colour forms. Their existence is therefore evidence that kiln control was already precise, which is a general truth about pigments: they tend to be records of how well a culture could control materials.

items.aliasZh: 玛雅蓝 · 玛雅蓝颜料
items.histZh: 玛雅蓝是中美洲特有的颜料，由靛蓝和一种叫坡缕石的黏土结合而成。它的稳定性在有机颜料里几乎不可思议：玛雅的壁画和祭器在热带雨林的高湿高温里放了上千年，蓝色还在。原理是靛蓝分子被锁进了黏土的纳米孔道里，被物理保护起来。屏幕上的玛雅蓝按壁画取色。
items.histEn: Maya blue is a pigment peculiar to Mesoamerica, made by binding indigo into a clay mineral called palygorskite. Its stability is almost implausible for an organic colourant: murals and offerings kept in tropical heat and humidity for over a thousand years still hold their blue. The reason is that the indigo molecules are locked inside nanoscale channels in the clay, protected physically rather than chemically. This sample follows mural work.
items.funZh: 玛雅蓝难做的地方在于：光把靛蓝和黏土混在一起不行，必须加热到一定温度才会「结合」进去，温度又不能让靛蓝分解 —— 中间只有很窄的一个窗口。这个配方在中美洲以外的文明里没有出现过。
items.funEn: Simply mixing indigo with the clay does not work. The two have to be heated, and within a narrow band of temperatures: warm enough for the indigo to enter the clay, cool enough that it does not decompose. Nothing comparable appears in any civilisation outside Mesoamerica.

items.aliasZh: 阴丹士林蓝 · 阴丹蓝
items.histZh: 阴丹士林蓝是 1901 年问世的还原染料，因为耐光耐洗到近乎夸张，在中国成了「永不褪色」的代名词 —— 民国时期风行一时的阴丹士林蓝布，就是这个染料染的。它比普鲁士蓝更沉、更灰，不带绿，是中国近现代日常生活里出现最多的蓝之一。屏幕上的值按老布样取色。
items.histEn: Indanthrone blue is a vat dye introduced in 1901 whose lightfastness and wash-fastness were so extreme that in China its name became a byword for colours that never fade. The indanthrene blue cloth widely worn in Republican-era China was dyed with it. Deeper and greyer than Prussian blue and without a green cast, it is among the most common blues of modern Chinese daily life. This value follows surviving cloth samples.
items.funZh: 「阴丹士林」在民国的上海几乎等于一种服装，学生、女工、职员都穿它，一时成了朴素和体面的标志。有意思的是，一个德国化工产品的商标名，最后变成了中国日常汉语里的一个颜色词，这在整个颜色词汇史上都不多见。
items.funEn: In Republican Shanghai the name stood for a whole way of dressing: students, factory women and clerks wore it, and it became a marker of both plainness and respectability. A German chemical trademark ending up as an everyday colour word in Chinese is a rare event in the history of colour vocabulary.

items.aliasZh: 法国群青 · 合成群青
items.histZh: 法国群青是 1826 年由法国人吉梅合成的群青，成分与天然青金石磨出的群青完全相同，价格却只有零头。它一出现就结束了天然的垄断 —— 在此之前，群青比等重的黄金还贵，画家签约时甚至会写明用多少群青。屏幕上的法国群青按 19 世纪产品取色，比天然品略偏紫。
items.histEn: French ultramarine was synthesised in 1826 by the Frenchman Guimet. Chemically identical to the ultramarine ground from lapis lazuli, it cost a fraction as much and ended the natural monopoly at a stroke. Before it, ultramarine had been more valuable by weight than gold, and painters wrote into their contracts how much of it they would use. This sample follows nineteenth-century production, slightly more violet than the natural article.
items.funZh: 合成群青的成功还留下一个副产品：它便宜到可以拿去洗衣服 —— 洗衣蓝就是用它做的，利用极淡的蓝抵消织物泛黄的观感。一种曾经只有圣母衣袍配用的颜料，最后进了洗衣盆。
items.funEn: Its success carried an odd side effect: it became cheap enough to put in the laundry. Laundry blue is made from it, a trace of blue cancelling the yellow cast of worn white cloth. A pigment once reserved for the Virgin's robe ended up in a wash tub.

items.aliasZh: 喹吖啶酮品红 · 喹红
items.histZh: 喹吖啶酮品红属于 1958 年才商业化的喹吖啶酮族，是 20 世纪有机颜料最重要的成果之一。它给出的是一种透明、偏冷的品红，在混色时特别有用 —— 用它加蓝可以调出干净的紫，而用暖红加蓝只会得到发脏的褐。屏幕上的值是近似值，真颜料的透明感更强。
items.histEn: Quinacridone magenta belongs to the quinacridone family commercialised in 1958, one of the most significant achievements of twentieth-century organic pigments. It supplies a transparent, cool magenta that is especially useful in mixing: with blue it makes a clean purple, whereas a warm red with blue only makes a muddy brown. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is more translucent still.
items.funZh: 品红在理论上是一种「不存在的颜色」：纯品红对应的是光谱上两端同时出现的波，人眼可以合成这种感觉，但没有任何单一波长的光看起来是品红。所以每一种品红颜料都是在骗视觉系统。
items.funEn: Magenta is, in a strict sense, a colour that does not exist: pure magenta corresponds to both ends of the spectrum arriving at once. The eye can synthesise the sensation, but no single wavelength looks magenta. Every magenta pigment is therefore a trick played on the visual system.

items.histZh: 喹吖啶酮紫是同族里色相更深的一支，介于品红和紫之间。它的意义在于补上了一个长期的空缺：古典绘画里的深紫一直靠含砷的染料或者昂贵的钴紫撑着，而喹吖啶酮紫既便宜又耐光。它还有个特点 —— 透明度高，罩染时会往底色里透。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Quinacridone violet is the deeper member of the family, sitting between magenta and violet. Its importance lies in filling a long-standing gap: deep purples in classical painting depended either on arsenic-bearing dyes or on expensive cobalt violets, and this one is both cheap and lightfast. It also has the property of being highly transparent, letting the underpainting show through a glaze. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 这类现代有机颜料的耐光等级大多是最高一档，实验室里用强光连续照射几百小时，颜色变化仍在仪器误差之内。所以鉴别一幅画是新作还是旧作时，颜料的老化程度有时反而帮不上忙 —— 现代颜料太抗老了。
items.funEn: Most modern organic pigments sit at the top lightfastness rating: hundreds of hours of intense exposure in the laboratory and the colour shift stays within instrument error. That is why pigment ageing sometimes cannot help in dating a painting. The modern materials simply refuse to age.

items.histZh: 汉莎黄是 1909 年德国开发的芳基黄类颜料，商号「Hansa」来自汉萨同盟，属于当时德国工业命名的一种习惯。它是第一批在价格和安全性上都压过传统黄颜料的产品 —— 不含铅、不含铬，却够亮够稳。今天它仍是水彩和水粉里最常见的黄之一。屏幕上的值是近似值，真颜料比这个略暖。
items.histEn: Hansa yellow is an arylide yellow developed in Germany in 1909, its trade name taken from the Hanseatic League in keeping with a naming habit of German industry at the time. It was among the first pigments to beat traditional yellows on both price and safety: no lead, no chromium, yet bright and stable enough to work. It remains one of the most common yellows in watercolour and gouache. The value shown is an approximation and slightly cooler than the real thing.
items.funZh: 芳基黄类颜料有个共同的短板：耐光性看具体品种，浅色调的比深色调的更容易褪。所以同样叫「汉莎黄」，深黄可能几十年不变，柠檬黄那一支却可能几年就淡下去 —— 同一个名字里藏着不同的命运。
items.funEn: Arylide yellows share a weakness: lightfastness varies by shade, and the paler grades fade sooner than the deeper ones. Two tubes labelled Hansa yellow can therefore behave completely differently, with the deep yellow holding for decades while the lemon grade pales within a few years. One name covering two fates.

items.histZh: 汉莎橙是汉莎黄族里色相偏深的一支，1910 年前后上市，用来替代铬橙之类含铅的暖色。它的透明度和着色力都不错，缺点是耐光性在浅色调时明显下降。屏幕上的值是近似值。它代表的其实是一整代「二十世纪初的合成暖色」—— 便宜、无毒、亮，但需要使用者了解哪种色调耐光差。
items.histEn: Hansa orange is the deeper member of the arylide family, marketed around 1910 as a replacement for lead-bearing warm colours such as chrome orange. Its transparency and tinting strength are both good, and its weakness is a clear drop in lightfastness at the pale end. The value shown is an approximation. It stands for a whole generation of early twentieth-century synthetic warms: cheap, non-toxic, bright, and asking the user to know which tints will not hold.
items.funZh: 二十世纪初的颜料替代潮有个规律：先替代含铅的，再替代含砷的，最后才轮到镉这类相对没那么急的。所以今天的调色盘上，留在老配方里的往往是镉，被换掉的多是铅 —— 安全性的优先级一直在变。
items.funEn: The replacement of pigments in the early twentieth century followed an order: lead first, then arsenic, and only later the less urgent cadmiums. That is why cadmium is the traditional metal most likely to survive on a modern palette while the leads were dropped — the ranking of what counts as dangerous keeps being revised.

items.histZh: 柠檬黄通常指铬酸钡那一支浅黄，色泽清冷发绿，跟镉黄那种暖黄正好站在两端。它的名字提示了颜料名的一条常见路子：拿水果当参照 —— 柠檬黄、樱桃红、杏黄、橙，都用日常能吃到的实物锚定色相。屏幕上的值是近似值，真颜料的偏绿程度更明显。
items.histEn: Lemon yellow usually refers to the barium chromate grade, a cool yellow with a green cast, standing at the opposite end from the warm cadmiums. The name illustrates a common way pigments get named: by anchoring the hue to fruit — lemon yellow, cherry red, apricot, orange. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is more visibly green.
items.funZh: 含铬的颜料整体上是安全的，除了铬酸铅那类可溶性的 —— 铬酸钡因为极难溶，反而属于较温和的一支。同一元素的化合物毒性可以差出几个量级，「含铬」三个字本身说明不了什么。
items.funEn: Chromium pigments are broadly safe apart from the soluble ones such as lead chromate; barium chromate is very nearly insoluble and therefore one of the gentler members. Toxicity within a single element can span orders of magnitude, so labelling something as containing chromium says very little on its own.

items.histZh: 锌黄是铬酸锌，工业上用得很广 —— 因为铬酸根有缓蚀作用，它长期是金属防锈底漆的主要成分。作为绘画颜料它偏冷、偏绿，着色力一般。有意思的是，同一个化合物在两个领域里的角色完全不同：在画布上是颜色，在钢板上是防腐蚀的屏障。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Zinc yellow is zinc chromate, and industry uses it widely: because the chromate ion inhibits corrosion it spent decades as the main ingredient of anti-rust primers. As a painting pigment it is cool, leaning green, with modest tinting strength. The same compound plays two entirely different roles — a colour on canvas, a barrier against rust on steel. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 铬酸锌的缓蚀原理和它的颜色有关：铬酸根在金属表面形成一层钝化膜，阻止进一步氧化。所以这类底漆的经典黄色并不是装饰选择，而是有效成分本身的颜色 —— 黄色只是它在工作。
items.funEn: The corrosion inhibition and the colour are connected: chromate forms a passivating film on the metal surface that halts further oxidation. The classic yellow of those primers is not a decorative choice but simply the colour of the active ingredient, doing its work.

items.histZh: 铬橙是碱式铬酸铅，与铬黄同族，只是碱度更高。它是 19 世纪最便宜的橙色颜料，用得极广 —— 从油画到油漆到印刷，但代价是含铅且见光会变暗。有趣的是，它变暗之后常常偏向红，所以老画上那些「橙色变红」的地方，多半是它在作怪。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Chrome orange is basic lead chromate, a relative of chrome yellow with more alkali in it. The cheapest orange of the nineteenth century, it went everywhere from oil painting to house paint to printing, at the cost of containing lead and darkening in light. Curiously, as it darkens it usually shifts toward red, so orange areas on old paintings that have turned red are often its doing.
items.funZh: 铬系颜料的变色是修复里公认的难题：变化发生在晶格内部，不是表面脏了，所以没法擦洗恢复，也不能靠上光解决。修复师能做的往往只是减缓它继续变，而不是把它变回去。
items.funEn: Colour change in chrome pigments is a recognised problem in conservation because it happens inside the crystal lattice rather than on the surface. It cannot be cleaned off and varnish will not fix it. All a conservator can usually do is slow it down, not reverse it.

items.histZh: 镉橙是硫化镉与硒化镉的固溶体，20 世纪初进入颜料市场，补上了镉黄和镉红之间的那个缺口。镉系颜料的特点是遮盖力强、耐光极好、色相纯正，代价是含镉，毒性明显。今天在欧盟等地，艺术家用镉颜料仍可买到，但工业用途已大幅受限。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Cadmium orange is a solid solution of cadmium sulfide and cadmium selenide, entering the pigment market in the early twentieth century and filling the gap between cadmium yellow and cadmium red. Cadmiums are opaque, extremely lightfast and hue-accurate, at the cost of containing cadmium and being clearly toxic. Artist-grade cadmiums are still sold in the EU and elsewhere, but industrial use has been heavily restricted. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 因为镉颜料既好看又有毒，颜料厂的做法是把它做成「不溶」的：颜料本身几乎不溶，所以只要不吸入粉尘、不误食，接触风险是可控的。这也是整个颜料毒性讨论里最容易被忽略的一点 —— 形态比成分更决定风险。
items.funEn: Because cadmiums are both good-looking and toxic, manufacturers make them insoluble: the pigment itself dissolves almost not at all, so the risk is manageable provided the dust is not inhaled and nothing is eaten. This is the most often overlooked point in arguments about pigment safety — form matters more than composition.

items.histZh: 镉绿严格说不是一种化合物，而是镉黄与酞菁绿（或氧化铬绿）的混合颜料。它的意义在于工业化预混：画家不必自己调，就能拿到一个颜色稳定、批次一致的绿。这类「颜料商预混色」在 20 世纪越来越多，也把「亲自调色」这件事从流程里挤出去了一部分。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Cadmium green is not a compound but a mixture, cadmium yellow blended with phthalo or chromium oxide green. Its interest lies in industrial pre-mixing: a painter could buy a stable, batch-consistent green without mixing it personally. Such manufacturer blends multiplied through the twentieth century and pushed the habit of mixing from scratch a little further out of the process. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 预混颜料的普及带来一个副作用：老画上那种「同一幅里绿有好几个微妙变体」的现象变少了。一管买来的绿就是一个绿，画家不再需要为了一个色相反复试调 —— 效率上去了，色域的层次却平了。
items.funEn: Pre-mixed pigments had a side effect: the several subtly different greens within a single old painting became rarer. A tube of green is one green, and the painter no longer has to hunt for a hue. Efficiency rose, and the tonal layering flattened.

items.histZh: 铬绿一般指氧化铬绿，19 世纪前期出现，是少数几种既耐高温、又耐酸碱、还完全不透明的绿。它不太适合直接当颜料正色，因为颜色闷、发灰，但它极稳定，所以在陶瓷釉料、防锈漆和需要长期暴露的场合里一直有用。屏幕上的值是近似值，真颜料更偏橄榄。
items.histEn: Chrome green usually means chromium oxide green, introduced in the early nineteenth century and one of the few greens that is simultaneously heat-resistant, acid-resistant, alkali-resistant and completely opaque. It is not well suited to being a principal colour, being dull and greyish, but its stability keeps it in ceramic glazes, anti-rust paints and any application exposed to the long term. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is more olive.
items.funZh: 氧化铬绿在钞票和邮票的印刷里地位很高 —— 因为它难仿，扫描打印时这个绿经常偏得离谱。所以今天很多钞票上还留着大块的绿，跟「钱是绿的」这个传统有关系，也跟防伪有关系。
items.funEn: Chromium oxide green has a standing in banknote and stamp printing because it imitates badly: scanners and printers routinely misread it. That is why so many notes still carry large green areas, a matter both of the old association between money and green and of simple anti-counterfeiting.

items.histZh: 铅丹是四氧化三铅，中国叫铅丹、西方叫 minium，罗马人还用它抄写标题，所以英文里「微型画」这个词跟它是同一个词根。它在中国既是颜料也是丹药，还大量用于木构建筑和船的防腐底漆。色偏橙红，遮盖力极强，缺点是含铅且见硫会变黑。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Red lead is lead tetroxide, called minium in the West, where Roman scribes used it for headings — which is why the English word for a miniature shares its root. In China it served as a pigment, as an ingredient in elixirs, and in quantity as a preservative primer on timber buildings and boats. The colour leans orange-red, the covering power is immense, and the drawbacks are lead content and a tendency to blacken on contact with sulfur. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 铅丹变黑的原理跟铅白类似：遇硫生成黑色的硫化铅。所以一幅用铅丹的画如果挂在有硫污染的环境里，橙红会一点点转暗 —— 有研究认为部分古画的「暗沉」并不是年代问题，而是环境问题。
items.funEn: Red lead blackens the same way lead white does, by forming black lead sulfide. A painting using it hung in a sulfur-rich environment therefore darkens progressively. Some of what is taken for the gloominess of age in older work has been argued to be an environmental effect rather than a matter of time.

items.histZh: 银朱是用汞和硫人工合成的硫化汞，成分与天然朱砂相同，但颗粒更细、颜色更艳，是古代最重要的红色颜料之一。它在中文文献里出现得很早，敦煌和明清建筑的彩画上都大量使用。银朱的问题和朱砂一样：含汞，长期接触有害，而且见光久了会由红转黑。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Silver vermilion is mercuric sulfide made synthetically from mercury and sulfur. Chemically the same as natural cinnabar, it is finer in grain and more vivid, and it ranks among the most important reds of the pre-modern world. It appears early in Chinese records and was used in quantity on Dunhuang material and on Ming and Qing architectural polychrome. Its problems match cinnabar's: it contains mercury, prolonged contact is harmful, and in light it eventually turns from red toward black.
items.funZh: 银朱的变黑是光化学过程，不是简单的褪色：硫化汞在光照下会转成另一种晶型，颜色由红变黑，而这个过程基本不可逆。所以博物馆里对含朱砂的织物和纸本，光照度控制得特别严。
items.funEn: The blackening is photochemical rather than simple fading: light converts mercuric sulfide to a different crystal form, turning the colour from red to black, and the change is essentially irreversible. It is why museums hold illuminance levels on cinnabar-bearing textiles and works on paper unusually low.

items.histZh: 朱膘是做朱砂时浮在最上面的那一层。朱砂研磨后用水漂，粗的沉底、细的浮上，上层颜色偏橙偏浅，就是朱膘，用来画脸部、花瓣这些需要透气的地方；下层浓艳，用来勾线、点花心。同一种矿，靠一次沉淀就被分成了两个色名。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Vermilion float is the fraction that rises to the top when cinnabar is ground and levigated in water. The coarse grains sink and the fine ones float, and the upper layer is lighter and more orange — used for faces and petals, places that need to breathe — while the dense lower layer is used for outlines and flower centres. One mineral, separated by a single settling, becomes two colour names. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 水飞法是中国传统颜料加工的核心工艺之一：靠反复研磨、悬浮、沉淀，把同一种矿物按颗粒大小分成好几个色阶。整个过程不用任何化学试剂，纯粹用物理手段分离 —— 朴素，但精度惊人。
items.funEn: Levigating in water was the core technique of traditional Chinese pigment preparation. Repeated grinding, suspension and settling sorted a single mineral into several grades by particle size, with no chemicals involved at all. Entirely physical, and remarkably precise.

items.histZh: 龙血是从龙血树属植物果实和树脂里得到的一种深红染料，中国的文献里叫「麒麟竭」，是进口货。它偏紫、偏暗，透明而发亮，古罗马和中国都拿它做漆器着色、也入药。名字来自它割开树皮后渗出的红色汁液，看上去像血。屏幕上的龙血是近似值。
items.histEn: Dragon's blood is a deep red dye obtained from the fruit and resin of Dracaena species. Chinese sources know it as qilin's blood, an imported article. It runs purplish and dark, transparent and glossy, and both Rome and China used it to colour lacquer and also as a medicine. The name comes from the red sap that bleeds out when the bark is cut, which looks like blood. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 龙血树最出名的一点是长得极慢、活得极长 —— 索科特拉岛上有些个体被测出超过一千年，是地球上寿命最长的有花植物之一。所以「龙血」这种染料在古代是奢侈品：原料来自少数几个地方，而且树不肯长快。
items.funEn: Dragon trees are famously slow and long-lived. Some individuals on Socotra have been dated at over a thousand years, among the oldest flowering plants on earth. The dye was accordingly a luxury: the raw material came from a handful of places and the tree refused to hurry.

items.histZh: 紫胶红来自紫胶虫 —— 一种寄生在树上的介壳虫，它分泌的树脂里带着红色素。印度、东南亚和中国南方都用它，既是染料也是虫胶漆的原料。它的红偏冷、偏玫，跟胭脂虫那种正红不是一个路子。屏幕上的值是近似值，实际染出的颜色随媒染剂变化很大。
items.histEn: Lac dye comes from the lac insect, a scale insect that lives on trees and secretes a resin containing a red colourant. India, Southeast Asia and southern China all used it, both as a dye and as the raw material for shellac. Its red leans cool and rosy, a different proposition from the crimson obtained from cochineal. The value shown is an approximation; what actually comes out of the dyebath varies greatly with the mordant.
items.funZh: 紫胶虫的这个分泌物还有个更有名的用途：虫胶。老式唱片之所以叫「虫胶唱片」，就是因为它压片用的材料来自这种虫子。所以同一只虫子，一身兼了染料、漆料和唱片三份工作。
items.funEn: The same secretion has a more famous second life as shellac, which is why early gramophone records were known as shellac discs: the material pressing them came out of this insect. One small creature supplying dye, varnish and records at once.

items.histZh: 茜素红是 1869 年由两位德国化学家合成出来的，成分与天然茜草根里的色素完全相同。它的意义在于：这是人类第一次把一种天然染料完整地人工合成出来 —— 在此之前，茜草要种两三年才能收根，之后欧洲的茜草田一片片改种了别的作物。屏幕上的茜素红是近似值，真颜料偏透明。
items.histEn: Alizarin crimson was synthesised in 1869 by two German chemists, chemically identical to the colouring matter in the madder root. Its significance is that this was the first time a natural dye was fully reproduced in the laboratory. Madder had taken two or three years of cultivation before the roots could be lifted, and within a generation European madder fields were being planted with other crops. The value shown is an approximation; the real pigment is more transparent.
items.funZh: 茜素红有个让画家头疼的缺点：耐光性其实一般，尤其是稀释之后。所以很多用它画的深红过了几十年会明显变浅、发粉。今天不少博物馆级的深红替代品，就是为了解决这个问题才被开发出来的。
items.funEn: Alizarin has a weakness that troubles painters: its lightfastness is only moderate, particularly when it is thinned. Deep reds painted with it visibly pale and turn pink over a few decades, and a number of museum-grade crimson substitutes were developed specifically to solve that.

items.aliasZh: 威尼斯红 · 威尼斯红土
items.histZh: 威尼斯红是一种偏暖的氧化铁红颜料，名字来自历史上威尼斯作为颜料集散地的地位，而不是产地。它比同族的印度红更暖、更偏橙，遮盖力强、耐光极好，是古典绘画里打底和画肉色的常用色。屏幕上的威尼斯红是近似值，不同矿源出来的差别不小。
items.histEn: Venetian red is a warm iron oxide red whose name records Venice's historical role as an entrepot for pigments rather than any place of origin. It runs warmer and more orange than its relative Indian red, with strong covering power and excellent lightfastness, and it was a standard colour for underpainting and flesh in classical practice. The value shown is an approximation; the variation between ore sources is considerable.
items.funZh: 含铁的土色是颜料史上最稳的一类：山洞壁画里几万年前的赭红，今天看还是红的。所以铁红系列的耐光性几乎不构成问题，画家挑它的理由不是耐久，而是色相和手感。
items.funEn: Iron-bearing earths are the most durable family in the history of pigments: ochre reds in cave paintings tens of thousands of years old are still red. Lightfastness is therefore almost never the reason a painter chooses one. The reasons are hue and handling.

items.histZh: 印度红也是一种氧化铁红，色相偏冷、偏紫，跟威尼斯红正好构成一对。名字的来路跟威尼斯红一样含糊，早期文献把它跟印度产的铁矿联系在一起，但后来这个名号基本成了某一档色相的通用称呼，跟产地没什么关系了。屏幕上的印度红是近似值。
items.histEn: Indian red is another iron oxide red, cooler and slightly more purple than Venetian red — the two form a matched pair. Its name is as vague in origin as its partner's: early sources associated it with ore from India, but the term long ago became a general label for a particular hue with no real geographic content. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 土色颜料名下这种「名字和产地脱钩」的现象很普遍：威尼斯红不定来自威尼斯，印度红不定来自印度，那不勒斯黄也早就不来自那不勒斯。色名一旦稳定下来，就变成了色相标签，产地信息被磨掉了。
items.funEn: Detachment of name from place is routine among earth pigments: Venetian red need not come from Venice, Indian red need not come from India, and Naples yellow stopped coming from Naples long ago. Once a colour name settles, it becomes a hue label and the geography wears off.

items.histZh: 铬锡红是氧化铬、氧化锡和氧化钙在高温下反应生成的红色发色体，18 世纪末就被用在陶瓷釉里。它的性格很特殊：在釉里能烧出稳定的粉红和玫红，而这些色相用别的方式极难在高温下保住。它只在陶瓷体系里成立，当不了普通绘画颜料。屏幕上的铬锡红按釉面取色。
items.histEn: Chrome-tin pink is a red colorant formed when chromium oxide, tin oxide and calcium oxide react at high temperature, in use in ceramic glazes from the late eighteenth century. Its behaviour is peculiar: inside a glaze it produces stable pinks and rose reds that are otherwise extremely difficult to preserve through a kiln firing. It exists only in ceramic systems and cannot serve as an ordinary painting pigment. This sample follows a glazed surface.
items.funZh: 这类色素叫「陶瓷色料」，跟颜料是两套逻辑：颜料要求颗粒细、能分散在油里；色料要求能扛住上千度的烧成，而且必须在釉里发色。同一个元素在两条路线上，能做出来的颜色完全不同。
items.funEn: Colorants like this belong to a separate discipline from pigments. A pigment has to be fine and dispersible in oil; a ceramic stain has to survive over a thousand degrees and develop its colour inside a glaze. The same element yields completely different colours along the two routes.

items.histZh: 熟赭是把生赭煅烧后得到的红棕颜料，色相比生赭深、偏红，透明度好。它在油画里用途极广：既能用来画大地和木头，也能当调色时的「降温剂」—— 想在鲜艳的颜色里掺一点旧感，加熟赭比加黑安全，因为黑会把颜色压脏，熟赭只会让它退一步。屏幕上的熟赭是近似值。
items.histEn: Burnt sienna is what an ochre becomes when it is calcined: a red-brown, deeper and redder than the raw earth, and notably transparent. It has an enormous range of use in oil painting, for ground and wood and, more delicately, as a cooling agent in mixtures — adding a trace of age to a bright colour is safer with burnt sienna than with black, since black muddies while burnt sienna only steps the colour back.
items.funZh: 「用黑调暗会脏，用熟赭调暗不会」几乎是油画的第一课。原因是黑把颜色的纯度一刀砍掉，而熟赭本身是有色相的暗，它在降低明度的同时保住了色相的方向，看起来就自然得多。
items.funEn: That black deadens a mixture while burnt sienna does not is roughly the first lesson in oil painting. Black simply removes saturation, whereas burnt sienna is a dark with a hue of its own: it lowers value while preserving the direction of the colour, which reads as natural.

items.histZh: 舍勒蓝是 1778 年由瑞典化学家舍勒制得的铜砷酸盐蓝色颜料，跟他后来做出的舍勒绿是同一路的产物 —— 都含砷。它一度被用来给纸和织物染色，也被画家使用，直到人们意识到砷的毒性之后才被淘汰。屏幕上的舍勒蓝是近似值。
items.histEn: Scheele's blue is a copper arsenite pigment prepared in 1778 by the Swedish chemist Scheele, a sibling of the Scheele's green he made later — both contain arsenic. It was used to dye paper and textiles and adopted by painters, and it was abandoned once the toxicity of arsenic was understood. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 舍勒蓝和舍勒绿的关系很能说明当年颜料化学的粗放：同一个人、同一类原料，配方稍微一动就从绿变蓝，而两者都含砷。那个年代的化学发现常常是先做出来、再慢慢发现它有害。
items.funEn: The relationship between Scheele's blue and his green says a lot about how rough early pigment chemistry was: one man, one family of ingredients, a small change in the recipe moving the result from green to blue, and arsenic in both. Discoveries of that era tended to be made first and found to be harmful later.

items.histZh: 桃黑是把桃核、杏核一类的果核烧成炭再磨细得到的黑颜料，中国和欧洲都有这种做法。它比灯黑偏暖、带一点褐，颗粒也粗一些，属于「低技术门槛」的颜料 —— 任何有果核和火的人都能做。传统颜料的很大一部分其实都是这种从厨房和窑里顺手长出来的东西。屏幕上的桃黑是近似值。
items.histEn: Peach black is made by charring peach and apricot stones and grinding the result fine, a practice found in both China and Europe. Warmer and slightly browner than lamp black, and coarser in grain, it belongs to the low-tech end of pigments: anyone with fruit stones and a fire can make it. A large part of the traditional palette consists of exactly this kind of thing, grown out of the kitchen and the kiln.
items.funZh: 炭黑一类的颜料的共同点是：原料决定了颗粒，颗粒决定了色调。果核炭偏暖、骨炭偏冷、油烟炭最黑。所以「黑」在传统颜料里从来不是一个颜色，而是一整排的颜色。
items.funEn: Carbon blacks share a rule: the source determines the grain, and the grain determines the tone. Fruit-stone char is warm, bone char cool, lamp soot the blackest. Black in the traditional palette is therefore never one colour but a whole row of them.

items.histZh: 灯黑是收集油脂燃烧时产生的烟灰得到的，是最古老的人造黑颜料之一。做法简单到近乎粗暴：拿个冷盘子架在油灯火焰上方，烟凝在盘底，刮下来就是。它的黑纯正、颗粒极细、遮盖力强，缺点是有油性、干得慢。屏幕上的灯黑是近似值。
items.histEn: Lamp black is collected from the soot of burning oil, and it is among the oldest artificial black pigments. The method is almost brutally simple: hold a cold plate over the flame, let the smoke condense, scrape it off. The black is clean, the grain extremely fine and the covering power high; the drawbacks are greasiness and slow drying. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 灯黑在中国还有个更有名的身份：墨。传统制墨就是把松烟或油烟收集起来，加胶、加香料，再反复捶打成锭。所以「灯黑」和「墨」本质上是一种东西，只是前者按颜料卖，后者按文具卖。
items.funEn: In China this same material has a far more famous identity: ink. Traditional ink-making collected pine or oil soot, bound it with glue and aromatics, and pounded it repeatedly into sticks. Lamp black and Chinese ink are essentially one substance, sold once as pigment and once as stationery.

items.histZh: 石墨灰取石墨的颜色，是带金属光的灰。石墨在颜料里用得不多 —— 因为它反光、不容易和其他颜料融合 —— 但它在另一条线上影响巨大：铅笔。16 世纪英国发现大块石墨矿之后，人们直接把它削成条裹上木头，铅笔就是这么来的，而「铅」字其实是个历史误会。屏幕上的石墨灰按普通铅笔芯取色。
items.histEn: Graphite grey is the colour of graphite, a grey with a metallic sheen. It is not much used as a pigment, since it reflects light and mixes poorly, but its influence runs down another line entirely: pencils. After a large graphite deposit was found in England in the sixteenth century, people simply sawed the material into rods and wrapped them in wood. The lead in pencil is a historical misunderstanding. This sample follows an ordinary pencil core.
items.funZh: 铅笔不含铅，但名字改不过来 —— 因为石墨刚被发现时被当成了铅的一种。更有意思的是，石墨和钻石都是纯碳，差别只在碳原子怎么排列：一个是最软的矿物之一，一个是已知最硬的。
items.funEn: Pencils contain no lead, but the name will not budge, because graphite was initially taken for a form of lead. More interesting still: graphite and diamond are both pure carbon. The only difference is how the atoms are arranged, which is the difference between one of the softest minerals known and the hardest.

items.histZh: 白垩是天然碳酸钙，由远古海洋微生物的钙质外壳沉积而成。它作为白色颜料用了很久，遮盖力不强、透明度高，所以更适合打底和做白色粉笔，而不是覆盖。它偏暖、偏土，跟锌白钛白那种冷白站得很远。屏幕上的白垩是近似值。
items.histEn: Chalk is natural calcium carbonate, laid down from the calcareous shells of microscopic marine organisms in the distant past. It has served as a white pigment for a very long time, with weak covering power and high transparency, which suits it to grounds and to white drawing sticks rather than to covering anything over. It runs warm and earthy, standing well away from the cool whites of zinc and titanium. The value shown is an approximation.
items.funZh: 白垩之所以叫这个名字，是因为它主要形成于白垩纪 —— 那个时期海洋里浮游生物极多，死后钙质壳大量沉降，堆成了后来整片整片的白色崖岸。所以「白垩」这个色名底下压着一亿年的生物沉积。
items.funEn: The Cretaceous period is named after chalk because microscopic marine life then was so abundant that its calcareous shells settled in enormous quantity, later forming entire white cliffs. Behind the colour word lies something close to a hundred million years of biological sediment.

items.histZh: 锌钡白是硫化锌与硫酸钡的混合物，1874 年前后问世，主要目的是绕开当时昂贵的锌白 —— 用便宜的硫酸钡把硫化锌「稀释」成一种价格可接受的白。它一度是最常用的工业白颜料，油漆、油墨、橡胶里都有。作为画家颜料它偏冷、遮盖力好，但耐酸差。屏幕上的值是近似值。
items.histEn: Lithopone is a mixture of zinc sulfide and barium sulfate, developed around 1874 essentially to get around the expense of zinc white: cheap barium sulfate dilutes the sulfide into an acceptable white at an acceptable price.
